title: ECO-MUSIC AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT—A NEW TOPIC WITHIN THE DISCIPLINE OF “MUSIC HISTORY” (THE GEORGIAN CASE)
venue: Innovations in Education: Prospects and Challenges of Today
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how new artistic works, specifically eco-music compositions, should be taught and analyzed within the discipline of music history. The author argues that traditional approaches to teaching music history are insufficient for a growing body of environmentally oriented compositions, and that a new methodology is needed to account for their artistic, scientific, ecological, and sustainable-development dimensions.

The paper does not study an intervention in the experimental sense. Instead, it proposes a conceptual framework for interpreting eco-music as both art and a response to ecological crisis. The Georgian context is central, with examples such as Eka Chabashvili’s works used to illustrate the emergence of eco-music in Georgia and its ties to scientific ideas, ecology, and broader cultural change.

The main conclusion is that eco-music should be examined not only through artistic, historical, and cultural lenses, but also in relation to sustainable development and its intersections with science. The paper suggests that this approach will help students understand the value and purpose of musical works more fully and recognize how music can contribute to environmental awareness and social responsibility.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual position paper without an empirical design, comparison group, or reported quantitative/qualitative study methods. It offers a pedagogical argument and examples rather than evidence of measured effects.
impact_tier_rationale: No intervention impact is evaluated quantitatively, so there is no measurable effect on learner or system outcomes. The paper is relevant to curriculum framing but does not demonstrate educational impact.

finding.finding_summary: This is a theoretical/overview article proposing that eco-music should be taught within music history as both an artistic and sustainability-related topic. It argues that such instruction would help students understand the value and purpose of musical works and their intersections with science and sustainable development, but reports no empirical effect sizes or sample-based outcomes.
finding.measure: Theoretical argument about curriculum content and interdisciplinary analysis of music works
